I would love to help you with that! We want to find the missing numerator so that two-thirds is equal to something over six. 

To get from 3 to 6 on the bottom, what did we multiply the 3 by?
It is 4/6 because you multiply the bottom by 2 so you have to multiply the top by 2 as well Next one: 2/9 + 4/9?

You are totally right about multiplying the top and bottom by 2! 

For your next question, we have two fractions with the exact same denominator: two-ninths plus four-ninths. Since the bottom numbers are already the same, what do we do with the top numbers to find our answer?
the answer is 6/9 because you just add the top numbers together and keep the bottom number the same Next one: 1/4 + 1/8?

Spot on! You keep the denominator the same and just add the numerators. 

Now for one-quarter plus one-eighth. Notice that the bottom numbers are different this time. Can you think of a way to change one-quarter so it has a denominator of eight, just like we did earlier?
